# Personal allowance and income tax bands, in plain English

<!-- Generated by `lake env lean --run Prose.lean` from UkTax/Rules/S35.lean. Do not edit: CI fails if this file differs from what the code prints. -->

Figures: 2026-27. The rules this text is printed from are proved equal to the model's own definitions for every input and every parameter set (`personalAllowanceRule_eval`, `mainRates_eval`); see [README.md](README.md) for what that does and does not cover.

## Personal allowance (ITA 2007 s35)

To work out your personal allowance:

1. Start with £12,570.
2. If your adjusted net income is more than £100,000, take off half of the amount by which it is more than £100,000 (£1 for every £2 over, worked out exactly rather than in whole £2 steps).
3. If that leaves less than £0, use £0.
4. If the result is not a whole number of pounds, round it up to the next whole pound.

**Adjusted net income** means your total income for the year that income tax is charged on, before any allowances, less the gross amount of any Gift Aid donations and of any pension contributions paid to a scheme that claims the tax relief for you.

For example:

| Adjusted net income | Your personal allowance |
| --- | --- |
| £90,000 | £12,570 |
| £100,000 | £12,570 |
| £100,001 | £12,570 |
| £110,001 | £7,570 |
| £120,000 | £2,570 |
| £125,140 | £0 |
| £150,000 | £0 |

## Income tax bands and rates (ITA 2007 s6 and s10)

Income tax on your taxable income is charged in bands. Each rate applies only to the part of your taxable income that falls in its band:

| Part of your taxable income | Rate |
| --- | --- |
| The first £37,700 | 20% (basic rate) |
| Over £37,700, up to £125,140 | 40% (higher rate) |
| Over £125,140 | 45% (additional rate) |

The £125,140 limit is not a figure of its own: it is twice the personal allowance (£12,570) plus the income at which the allowance starts to be taken away (£100,000). So it is the income at which the allowance has all gone, and it moves whenever either of those changes.

**Taxable income** means your income for the year after your personal allowance has been taken off. These bands are for earnings, pensions, rent and other income that is not savings or dividends, for someone who is not a Scottish taxpayer.

For example:

| Taxable income | Income tax |
| --- | --- |
| £12,000 | £2,400 |
| £37,700 | £7,540 |
| £50,000 | £12,460 |
| £125,140 | £42,516 |
| £200,000 | £76,203 |
